content:
The image shows a soybean leaf (upper surface) covered with numerous small, irregularly shaped dark brown to reddish-brown lesions scattered uniformly across the surface. Key observations:

- Lesions are small, discrete, and dark brown
- Shape is irregular to roughly circular
- No gray centers (ruling out Frogeye)
- No yellow-green halos (ruling out Bacterial Blight)
- No obvious pustules or spore masses on this surface (ruling out Soybean Rust)
- Some lesions appear to be coalescing into slightly larger blotches
- Lesions present on what appears to be the upper leaf surface

This pattern — numerous small, dark brown, irregularly shaped lesions distributed across the leaf — is classic for Septoria brown spot (caused by *Septoria glycines*), which matches the description: "small, irregularly shaped dark brown lesions on both leaf surfaces that can merge into larger blotches."
